nonlow_rows.exact_scope: In the finite-chain setting, P is irreducible and aperiodic. For every starting state x there exists a strong stationary time tau such that s_x(t)=P_x(tau>t) for all t>=0.
actual_author_mechanism: Fix x and define a_t=min_y P^t(x,y)/pi(y)=1-s_x(t). The author first derives the necessary time/state mass pi(y)(a_t-a_(t-1)), not merely a desired marginal stopped law.
Use the post-stopping factorization(6.4) to identify previously stopped mass at current state y as pi(y)a_(t-1); the available surviving mass at y is P^t(x,y)-pi(y)a_(t-1).

Divide the needed new stopped mass by that surviving mass to obtain a state-and-time-specific conditional stopping hazard (a_t-a_(t-1))/(P^t(x,y)/pi(y)-a_(t-1)). Its bound comes from the minimum-ratio definition and monotonicity, not from a background optimal-SST theorem.

Independent Uniform[0,1] variables implement the conditional hazards along the trajectory. The induction uses the full time/state identity(6.21) and transports the prior stopped mass through the Markov kernel.
Summing the resulting matched state masses gives P_x(tau<=t)=a_t, the optimal separation tail for every time, a.s. finiteness from a_t->1, and strong stationarity from the joint factorization.
